articles.title: Extinction risks in deep-sea populations revealed by genomic data and ecological niche modeling
Autapse-inspired neuromorphic hardware with synapse–neuron integration for bidirectional feedback control
articles.abstract: Abstract Establishing autonomous and energy-efficient feedback control at the hardware level remains challenging because conventional systems rely on centralized processing and continuous external computation, increasing energy consumption and system complexity. Here we show a neuromorphic autapse-inspired system that enables localized and bidirectional feedback control, using thermoregulation as a representative application. An autapse is a self-synaptic connection in which a neuron feeds its output back to its own synaptic input, enabling intrinsic feedback modulation. The system integrates a solid electrolyte-based synaptic transistor capable of multiplexing multiple inputs and a bidirectional leaky integrate-and-fire artificial neuron. By feeding the neuronal output back to an additional synaptic gate, excitatory and inhibitory feedback loops are realized within a compact architecture. Using an artificial thermoregulation platform, temperature-dependent inputs bidirectionally modulate neuronal firing frequency, demonstrating biologically inspired feedback control with a compact set of neuromorphic devices for autonomous and energy-efficient systems.

articles.title: Evolution of the molybdenum and vanadium cycles through time and their impact on ancient nitrogen fixation
SIP-enabled multi-omics reveals soil microbiome responses to drought and rehydration
A prefrontal microcircuit computes trial-wise discount of reinforcement during threat learning in male mice
Phylogeographic and functional assembly of population-level bacterial immunity
Cobalt based anode for highly stable alkaline water electrolysis under operation conditions beyond industrial requirements
Scaling medical imaging report generation with multimodal reinforcement learning
articles.abstract: Abstract In medical imaging report generation, supervised fine-tuning can overfit to superficial patterns and generalize poorly across institutions. We introduce Universal Report Generation (UNIRG), which adopts reinforcement learning to directly optimize clinically meaningful quality criteria. With this framework, we developed UNIRG-CXR, an 8-billion-parameter vision–language model trained on four public datasets (MIMIC-CXR, CheXpert Plus, ReXGradient-160k and IU-Xray) by supervised fine-tuning followed by reinforcement learning (group-relative policy optimization) against a composite lexical, semantic and clinical-error reward. We evaluated held-out test sets and an external proprietary dataset, with RadCliQ as primary metric and expert radiologist validation. Here we show that our method improves report quality and generalization: UNIRG-CXR surpasses prior models on the ReXrank benchmark across four datasets and two generation settings, exceeding the previous best score by over 50% on two test sets, and produces fewer clinically significant errors while maintaining performance on unseen data sources and across demographic subgroups.

articles.title: Latitude modulates climate-driven maize yield gains across the central U.S. “warming hole”
articles.abstract: Abstract Maize yield responses to climate change differ seasonally and regionally, with both positive and negative impacts shaped by local climate trends and management decisions. Here, using a phenology-aligned moving crop-season framework and the Hybrid-Maize model (1991–2024) across five U.S. Corn Belt states, we quantify climate-driven yield contributions and show that they transition from southern declines to northern gains, reflecting the persistent influence of the central U.S. summer warming hole characterized by cooling maximum temperatures and increasing rainfall. A systematic thermal mismatch between environmental heat availability and hybrid growing degree day requirements is observed, particularly south of 42°N, where thermal matching declined despite favorable thermal conditions. Contrasting trends in thermal matching and reproductive duration help explain the latitude-dependent structure of climate-driven yield contributions. Our findings highlight how hybrid selection modulates the impacts of temperature, precipitation, vapor pressure deficit, and radiation trends on maize yield gains across the U.S. Corn Belt.

articles.title: Thin-film lithium niobate waveguide-integrated p-i-n Tungsten selenide photodiodes with 10Gbit/s data reception
articles.abstract: Abstract Thin-film lithium niobate (TFLN) is a promising photonic platform in next-generation integrated optoelectronics and on-chip/chip-chip interconnection due to its attractive optical property and versatility. However, integration of conventional-material-based photodetectors on TFLN platforms still faces multiple challenges. Herein, a high-bandwidth TFLN-based waveguide-integrated lateral WSe 2 p-i-n photodetector is presented. The localized self-aligned doping process eliminates slow carrier diffusion and defect trapping in doped regions which further boosts modulation bandwidth. Secondly, n-type and p-type Ohmic contacts, along with a high-quality p-n junction, are achieved through Se vacancy defect engineering and high-work function molybdenum oxide buffer layer, respectively. Furthermore, combined with the high dielectric constant of lithium niobate suppressing ionized impurity scattering, carrier mobilities exceeding 350 cm 2 /V·s are achieved for both electrons and holes, significantly accelerating carrier drift. The device features a measured bandwidth of 1.12 GHz and a data rate up to 10 Gbit/s in visible light. Separately, the device achieves a responsivity of ~492 mA·W −1 and a near-unity external quantum efficiency of 95.6% at 638 nm. This combination of two-dimensional homostructure and TFLN nano-waveguides provides a basis for high-speed photodetectors and visible-light interconnections in future TFLN integrated optoelectronics and optical input/output applications.

articles.title: Epigenetic gatekeeping enables genome-scale horizontal gene transfer in eukaryotic cells
Structural basis of ligand-mediated transition to higher-order rubisco assemblies
articles.abstract: Abstract Proteins often assemble as higher order complexes, underlying a diversity of molecular structures and biological functions. The emergence of protein-protein interactions between binding partners is generally considered to be the primary driver of oligomerization. However, ligand binding has also been demonstrated to affect higher-order assembly, though this phenomenon is not widely considered as a primary driver of oligomerization. Here, we describe the mechanism by which different rubisco oligomeric states are induced via ligand binding. By expanding the phylogenetic sampling of a unique clade of rubisco, we discover a range of oligomeric responses to ligand binding across the phylogeny and identify the structural features responsible for shifts in the oligomeric state that ultimately provide a path to evolving new quaternary structures. Here, we identify a ligand-dependent mechanism giving rise to new protein assemblies, in contrast with the typical process of evolving new protein-protein interfaces directly. Our findings describe a means by which binding and entrenchment of a ligand enables an increase in structural complexity.

articles.title:
Impacts of Biological
Filtration on Disinfection Byproduct
Control during Drinking Water Purification: A Critical Review
articles.abstract: Abstract Biofiltration, particularly biological activated carbon and sand filtration, is widely implemented as a low-chemical, energy-efficient barrier to attenuate disinfection byproduct (DBP) precursors. However, biofilters are living, time-evolving ecosystems that can transition from a net “sink” to a net “source” of reactive precursors. This review synthesized evidence that biofiltration exhibits selective removal: hydrophobic and high-molecular-weight C-DBP precursors are preferentially removed, whereas hydrophilic N-DBP (e.g., HANs, NDMA) precursors readily break through and may be newly produced. The authors clarified the mechanistic basis of precursor generation, highlighting (i) biofilm turnover that releases intracellular organic matter enriched in amines and nucleic acids, (ii) continuous production and sloughing of soluble microbial products and extracellular polymeric substances that elevate protein-like DON, and (iii) media aging and stratification that diminish removal efficacy. Regression analysis estimated sink–source transition for N-DBP precursor removal at approximately log10(bed volumes) = 5.38 (∼240,000 bed volumes), a practical reference in drinking water treatment plants. Furthermore, the authors identified critical operational tipping points, including oxidant pre-exposure, temperature fluctuations, and nutrient stoichiometry, that can trigger this functional inversion. Finally, a risk-oriented framework is proposed, advocating for precursor-specific monitoring (e.g., fluorescence signatures) and intelligent process control to stabilize biofilter performance against emerging genotoxic risks.

articles.title:
Evaluating Pollution
Prevention Effectiveness for
Toxic Substances in Canada Using Advanced Difference-in-Differences
Methods
articles.abstract: Abstract This study evaluates the effectiveness of pollution prevention (P2) activities using facility-level data from Canada’s National Pollutant Release Inventory (NPRI) over 1993–2024. Leveraging recent advances in causal inference methodology that account for staggered treatment adoption and heterogeneous treatment effects, this Difference-in-Differences (DiD) analysis moves beyond conventional DiD to identify substantial heterogeneity in P2 impacts across time, sectors, regions, P2 activities, and substances. Key findings indicate analysis of staggered adoption matters, with cohort-specific release reductions ranging widely, and larger effects among earlier adoption cohorts (2001–2003 ∼0-76 vs 2021 ∼3%). P2 adoption is associated with an average 19% reduction in pollutant releases. In contrast, P2 activities are associated with a near-zero and statistically insignificant increase in waste. P2 is more effective for releases to water, and within specific sectors such as Mining and Quarrying and Conventional Oil and Gas extraction. Stronger effects are observed for activities related to Inventory Management/Purchasing, and in Ontario, Alberta, and Quebec, and for VOCs. Despite study limitations, the results suggest that P2 delivers net environmental benefits overall and highlight the importance of modern causal inference methods for evaluating P2 policies in settings with staggered treatment adoption, such as the NPRI.

articles.title:
Turning
Abandoned
Mines into Carbon Sinks: Laboratory
Demonstration of CO2 Hydrate Sequestration in Cold-Region
Goafs under Permafrost Conditions
articles.abstract: Abstract Carbon capture, utilization, and storage (CCUS) is a key technology for carbon neutrality, but conventional CO2 geological sequestration suffers from high injection pressure, limited stability, and restricted storage space. Hydrate-based CO2 sequestration offers high capacity, low cost, and intrinsic safety. This study proposes a novel in situ CO2 hydrate formation and sequestration method in coal mine goafs containing permafrost layers in cold regions. The natural low-temperature permafrost environment provides favorable conditions for hydrate formation, while goafs offer large storage space. To avoid hydrate plugging and improve engineering feasibility, a liquid-first CO2 constant-pressure supply and predissolution mode was adopted. We simulated goaf conditions at depths of 110–130 m and ∼1 MPa. Experiments tested three injection temperatures (293.15, 298.15, and 303.15 K) and five goaf temperatures (269.15–277.15 K) using tetrahydrofuran and tryptophan as promoters. Results proved efficient sequestration at a low pressure of 1 MPa. Under optimal conditions (injection temperature of 298.15 K, goaf temperature of 271.15 K), capacity reached 60.9 mmol of CO2/mol of water (mmol/mol) with an efficiency of 135.36 (kg·m–3)/MPa. The 26.7 h stability experiments under depressurization showed 4.21–16.09 mmol/mol dissociated initially, but 66.38%–90.77% CO2 remained sequestered. Further, one-month tests under the pressure-release condition revealed hydrate dissociation almost stopped after day 1, yielding a 65.32% permanent sequestration ratio. Crucially, under the pressure-maintained condition, the system continued to form CO2 hydrates over the 30-day period, resulting in an additional 31.04% CO2 storage. These results validate the feasibility and long-term stability of this novel approach.

articles.title:
Strategies for Eliminating
Heavy Air Pollution in
the Beijing–Tianjin–Hebei Region: Insights from Joint
Practices during the 2022 Olympic and Paralympic Winter Games
articles.abstract: Abstract The 2022 Olympic Winter Games (OWG) and Paralympic Winter Games (PWG) marked the first time the Beijing–Tianjin–Hebei (BTH) region implemented joint air pollution prevention and control measures for a winter mega-event. Notably, while Beijing maintained clean air (daily PM2.5 concentration ≤ 75 μg/m3, according to the Ambient Air Quality Standards in effect at the time) during the OWG, a heavy-pollution episode occurred during the PWG, with the 24-h average PM2.5 concentration peaking at 155 μg/m3. Combining field observations, dynamic emission characterization, and The Comprehensive Air quality Model with extensions (CAMx) simulations, we conducted a closed-loop study to investigate the underlying causes of this episode. Results show that while the industrial sector effectively regulated emissions, the mobile-source activity levels recovered rapidly after the Chinese New Year, outweighing the control measures implemented for mobile sources. This recovery increased total NOx emissions by 13% in the BTH region, driving nitrate-dominated PM2.5 pollution. During the study period, the PM2.5 nitrate concentration (normalized by the carbon monoxide concentration) was found to increase by 3 × 10–4 and 1 × 10–5 for each one-ton increase in NOx emissions in Beijing and the BTH region, respectively. To eliminate heavy PM2.5 pollution under the meteorological conditions observed during the PWG, NOx emissions would need to be further reduced by ≥1% in Beijing and ≥7% in the BTH region. This work underscores the urgent need to mitigate emissions from diesel trucks and nonroad machinery, especially under extremely adverse meteorological conditions in the BTH region.

articles.title:
Gradient-Charge
Oxygen Vacancy Pairs Enable Synergistic
Activation of O2 and H2O for Low-Temperature
CH3CN Emission Control
articles.abstract: Abstract Acetonitrile (CH3CN) emitted from industrial production severely threatens atmospheric quality due to its persistence and high toxicity. While selective catalytic oxidation (SCO) represents the most promising technology for CH3CN elimination, the inherent competition between O2-activated oxidation and H2O-activated hydrolysis pathways has long prevented the simultaneous achievement of excellent low-temperature activity and high N2 selectivity. Herein, we report a Cu-modified TiO2 catalyst and propose a Cu-induced gradient-charge oxygen vacancy pair structure (Ti–OVR–Cu–OVP–Ti) as the most plausible active site configuration that enables activation of O2 and H2O via electron filling of their antibonding orbitals to promote the reaction during CH3CN oxidation. The electron-rich OVR site can adsorb both O2 and H2O, donating electrons to populate the π* antibonding orbital of O2 and the σ* antibonding orbital of H2O. Meanwhile, the electron-poor OVP site adsorbs O2 or H2O and serves as a reservoir to sustain a continuous supply of active species. The optimized catalyst induced by Ti–OVR–Cu–OVP–Ti structure achieves complete CH3CN conversion at 220 °C with 96% N2 selectivity. This work highlights the critical role of electron configuration in tailoring oxygen vacancy functions, providing a general strategy for developing advanced environmental catalysts for practical CH3CN emission control.

articles.title:
A Scenario-Based
Probabilistic First-Tier Screening
of Potential Chemical Risk to European Groundwater Ecosystems
articles.abstract: Abstract Groundwater supplies much of the freshwater used by humans while supporting highly specialized biological communities characterized by high endemism and limited taxonomic, functional, and phylogenetic redundancy. Yet European Union groundwater legislation remains resource-oriented and addresses the ecological consequences of chemical contamination only indirectly. We conducted a continent-wide, first-tier screening of potential chemical risk to European groundwater ecosystems. Harmonized European surface water and groundwater monitoring data were combined with geostatistical interpolation and transport modeling to estimate contaminant concentrations at the groundwater table, while uncertainty in hydrogeological conditions, chemical fate, and preferential transport was propagated through Monte Carlo simulations. We compared a Surface Water Baseline scenario, based on model-derived groundwater concentrations and existing freshwater regulatory thresholds, with a Groundwater-Informed Conservative scenario integrating measured groundwater concentrations, groundwater-fauna toxicity data, and precautionary adjustments where groundwater-specific evidence was unavailable. Potential risk was summarized as the average frequency of exceedance (AFE) across contaminants and uncertainty realizations; its maps indicate the frequency and spatial distribution of threshold exceedances, not their magnitude or the severity of ecological damage. Mean AFE was low under the baseline scenario but increased 5-fold under the conservative scenario, revealing areas in the medium-to-very-high screening classes in the Pyrenean–Catalan sector, Sierra Nevada, and the eastern Balkan–Carpathian region. The framework provides a replicable basis for prioritizing monitoring, ecotoxicological testing, and management.

articles.title:
Near-Real-Time
Mapping of Seamless All-Hour Aerosol
Optical Depth in China
articles.abstract: Abstract Aerosol optical depth (AOD) is central to assessing aerosol climate forcing and air quality, yet persistent cloud cover and the absence of nighttime satellite retrievals preclude seamless, all-hour monitoring. Here, we develop an automated machine-learning framework that fuses a newly available gridded visibility data set with forecast AOD and spatiotemporal covariates to reconstruct AOD over China at an hourly 5 km resolution in near-real-time. Trained on geostationary satellite observations, the model achieves robust performance (Pearson correlation coefficient R = 0.95 in cross-validation) and outperforms reanalysis and forecast products while filling cloud- and darkness-induced gaps. Independent validation against MODIS and ground-based nighttime Aerosol Robotic Network (AERONET) measurements yields consistent accuracy (MODIS R = 0.61 and AERONET R = 0.76), confirming physical generalizability. The resulting seamless record exposes a pronounced diurnal cycle with a midday minimum and an early morning maximum, and documents a consistent year-on-year decline from 2020 to 2022 that aligns with China’s clean-air actions and COVID-19 lockdowns. During a record-breaking dust storm, the framework tracks aerosol dynamics during cloud-obscured and nocturnal phases, capturing an uninterrupted process-level account of the event. By delivering the day–night aerosol continuum at high resolution and low latency, this work bridges a critical observational gap in air-quality response, data assimilation, and diurnal aerosol-climate research.

articles.title:
Nanoconfinement
Controls Hydrogen Transport in Shales
articles.abstract: Abstract Underground hydrogen storage (UHS) in sedimentary formations requires understanding how hydrogen migrates, persists, and is released under nanoscale confinement in fine-grained rocks that may act as reservoirs or caprocks. Here, we combine in situ small-angle neutron scattering (SANS) with molecular dynamics simulations to examine how wetting state controls hydrogen reversibility and postcycling pore occupancy in shale nanopores. SANS-derived pore-size distributions reveal a clear hierarchy: dry shale exhibits near-complete reversibility, decane-saturated shale shows partial recovery, and water-saturated shale displays minimal recovery, with persistent postcycling occupancy concentrated in pores <2 nm. Molecular simulations support a mechanistic interpretation in which this hierarchy arises from coupled nanoscale effects, including cavity-formation penalties, confinement-induced stress anisotropy, and fluid-specific interfacial free-energy barriers at mineral and organic surfaces. Water-saturated nanopores are associated with strong thermodynamic and mechanical constraints consistent with reduced hydrogen reversibility, whereas these constraints are substantially weaker in dry pores and intermediate in decane-filled pores. Together, the experimental and molecular simulation results provide a framework linking nanoscale fluid–rock interactions to hydrogen hysteresis and retention, with implications for subsurface hydrogen recoverability and containment in underground storage systems.

articles.title:
Spectroscopic
Insights into Ion Pairing in Sulfate
Electrolytes: Implications for Sorption in Aqueous Systems
articles.abstract: Abstract Ion pairing, including contact, solvent-shared, and solvent-separated ion pairs (CIPs, SIPs, and SSIPs, respectively), affects aqueous reaction chemistry, sorption, and precipitation processes. Accurate characterization of ion pairing in aqueous sulfate electrolytes is essential for understanding their thermodynamics and hydration structure, yet comprehensive quantification across aqueous and mixed-solvent systems remains limited. We combine Raman spectroscopy with dielectric spectroscopy, using waveguide-based setups (WR-62 and WR-28, applied for the first time) and a broadband probe station (10 MHz–50 GHz), to characterize ion pairing and solvent–solute interactions in monovalent cation sulfate salts in water and water/methanol solutions. Dielectric spectroscopy resolved SSIP and SIP fractions, with SSIPs dominating Li2SO4 and Na2SO4. Raman spectroscopy quantified CIPs (K2SO4 > Na2SO4 ≈ Li2SO4), consistent with cation hydration and polarizability. Methanol increased SIP and CIP concentrations. Ion association stability constants and mean activity coefficients were calculated with Archer’s form of the Pitzer model, incorporating short-range binary and ternary ion–ion interactions. This approach predicts mean activity coefficients at elevated ionic strengths without double-counting ion-pairing contributions, enabling determination of stability constants and aqueous speciation. Resolving ion-pair speciation is important for accurate thermodynamic models of sulfate-bearing waters relevant to membrane separations and resource recovery.

articles.title:
TP-Agent: An Auditable
LLM Agent for Predicting Pollutant
Transformation Products in Oxidative Water Treatment
articles.abstract: Abstract Predicting the transformation products (TPs) of organic micropollutants is important for characterizing their chemical fate during oxidative water treatment and prioritizing candidate structures for high-resolution mass spectrometry (HRMS) analysis. Limited labeled data and diverse reaction pathways make this task challenging. TP-Agent combines a large language model (LLM), training-only analog retrieval, and executable atom/bond edits to rank TP candidates with inspectable structural records. On 231 standardized-parent-disjoint reactions, TP-Agent achieved 78.8% strict Top-5 accuracy, compared with 65.8% for the bare LLM, 76.2% for standalone retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), and 56.3 ± 1.5% for TP-Transformer across three training seeds. Parent-clustered bootstrap analysis supported the gain over the bare LLM; the 2.6-percentage-point difference from RAG was not statistically significant. Retrieval supplied most of the accuracy gain, while graph execution added candidate-linked structural records. Among 1095 candidates, 92.7% had exact edit-replay or deterministic-projection records, measuring structural linkage rather than mechanistic validity. Where available, candidate-linked LLM rationales provide chemical hypotheses for inspection. Estimated parallel latency and API-equivalent cost were 3.5 and 7.4 times those of RAG, respectively. TP-Agent thus combines TP candidate ranking with traceable structural operations and inspectable chemical hypotheses for HRMS follow-up.

articles.title:
Aldehyde-philic
Portal Engineering of γ-Cyclodextrin
MOF for Synergistic Capture of Toluene and Formaldehyde in Humid Atmospheric
Environments
articles.abstract: Abstract Efficient removal of multicomponent volatile organic compounds (VOCs) from real environments remains challenging, particularly under humidity. This study introduces an “aldehyde-philic portal modification” strategy that precisely anchors dopamine (DA) at γ-cyclodextrin-based metal–organic framework (γ-CD-MOF) outer rim via H-bonding to construct oligomeric polydopamine (o-PDA) structures. This pore design partitions the cyclodextrin cavity into an aldehyde-philic outer rim and arene-philic interior for efficient synergistic capture of formaldehyde and toluene in humidity. Exposed pyrrolic N sites on o-PDA enable γ-CD-MOF@PDA2 to preferentially bind CH2O, which then act as new sites to enhance subsequent C7H8 capture via CH−π interactions while hindering H2O binding to peripheral hydroxyls and preventing large-sized water clusters from blocking cavity openings. Furthermore, the hydrophobic inner cavity exhibits strong π–π conjugation with C7H8, facilitating its diffusion and establishing an “outer capture–inner fixation” pathway, significantly enhancing toluene capacity. At ∼40% relative humidity, the toluene working capacity of γ-CD-MOF@PDA2 in the multicomponent system increased by 106% over the single-component system, while the formaldehyde capacity remained unchanged. Consequently, the total working capacity of toluene and formaldehyde reached twice the sum of their single-component adsorption capacities, demonstrating marked synergistic coadsorption. This work provides a feasible approach for controlling multicomponent VOCs in complex humid atmospheric environments.

articles.title:
Global Analysis
and Prediction of Bicarbonate in Groundwater
under Climate Change
articles.abstract: Abstract Bicarbonate (HCO3–) is a major contributor to the alkalinity of groundwater, and low concentrations can reduce buffering capacity and increase the potential susceptibility of water to corrosion-related quality deterioration, particularly in untreated groundwater systems with corrosion-prone infrastructure. Here, we use machine learning and a comprehensive data set of 28,902 groundwater samples from 80 countries to produce a global probability map of HCO3– concentrations below 80 mg/L and estimate the population residing within the Low-Alkalinity Corrosion Risk Potential Zone (LACRPZ). From 2000 to 2020, LACRPZ was mainly concentrated in Southeast Asia and South America, with approximately 704 million people residing within these zones, particularly in Oceania (52.92%) and South America (35.09%). Although the area of LACRPZ is projected to decline under future climate change, the resident population in LACRPZ is expected to increase. This study reveals the evolution of global groundwater bicarbonate concentrations and resident population, underscoring the importance of integrating bicarbonate into water safety management strategies.

articles.title:
Maternal 6PPD-Quinone
Exposure is Associated with
Infant Neurodevelopmental Delay: Epidemiological Evidence and Mechanistic
Insights from a Birth Cohort Study
articles.abstract: Abstract Tire-derived p-phenylenediamines (PPDs) and their quinone derivatives (PPD-Qs) have emerged as potential neurotoxicants, yet the associations of prenatal exposure with offspring neurodevelopment remain underexplored. Therefore, we conducted a nested case-control study within a prospective birth cohort (n = 1,317) and measured ten urinary PPDs/PPD-Qs at 6–16 weeks of gestation. In the primary adjusted model, higher urinary concentrations of 6PPD-quinone (6PPD-Q) and N,N′-di(o-tolyl)-p-phenylenediamine (DTPD) were associated with higher odds of neurodevelopmental delay. Quantile g-computation further indicated that a simultaneous one-quartile increase in all components of the PPDs/PPD-Qs mixture was associated with higher odds of neurodevelopmental delay (odds ratio = 1.33, 95% confidence interval: 1.03–1.72). Random forest analysis identified 6PPD-Q as having the highest variable importance among the measured PPDs/PPD-Qs. Network toxicology analysis implicated dopaminergic, serotonergic, and glutamatergic neurotransmission pathways as potentially relevant to 6PPD-Q-associated neurodevelopmental toxicity. In bEnd.3 mouse brain microvascular endothelial cells, 6PPD-Q exposure induced transcriptomic alterations involving xenobiotic metabolism, inflammatory signaling, and neurotransmission-related pathways. These changes were accompanied by decreased mRNA expression of the blood–brain barrier tight junction–related genes ZO-1 and occludin. Collectively, these epidemiological associations and complementary mechanistic findings support the biological plausibility of 6PPD-Q-associated developmental neurotoxicity and warrant further investigation and independent replication.

articles.title: Ferrocene heteroconjugation enables charge transport in DNA monolayers
Robust optical skyrmion arising from randomness
Pigment repression protects fungus from ferroptosis to maintain virulence
ATR promotes genome instability via CENP-A eviction from centromeres after prolonged exposure to genotoxic stress
Nudix protein D250R promotes African swine fever virus infection by disrupting host ubiquitination machinery
Probing topological edge states in a molecular synthetic dimension
articles.abstract: Abstract Synthetic dimensions, where additional spatial dimensions are encoded within the internal states of a quantum system, allow the realisation of phenomena usually inaccessible in experiments. Ultracold polar molecules are an ideal platform for synthetic dimensions, providing large Hilbert spaces of long-lived rotational and hyperfine states that can be linked with microwave fields to simulate tunnelling. Here, we realise a one-dimensional synthetic lattice using the rotational states of ultracold RbCs molecules and investigate the topological properties of the Su-Schrieffer-Heeger model. We spectroscopically probe the system using an auxiliary rotational state and study the time dynamics after deterministic state preparation. We demonstrate long coherence times, reaching ~ 500 tunnelling periods even for lattices spanning eight rotational states. Using full site-resolved readout over long evolution times, we study the robustness of topologically protected edge states against perturbations that preserve or break chiral symmetry. These results establish ultracold molecules as a powerful platform for quantum simulation using synthetic dimensions.

articles.title: Near-infrared plasmonic response in hyperdoped silicon nanoantennas for all-silicon photodetection
articles.abstract: Abstract Plasmonic materials enable subwavelength confinement of light through the collective response of free carriers, but their operational spectral range is typically constrained by intrinsic carrier densities. Hyperdoped semiconductors offer a route to engineer plasmonic properties within a CMOS-compatible platform, yet their plasmonic response in silicon remains largely limited to the mid-infrared. Here we show that nanoantenna engineering extends the plasmonic response of phosphorus-hyperdoped silicon toward the near-infrared. The nanoantenna arrays exhibit tunable, polarization-dependent resonances in the 1–2 μm range, arising from geometry-driven localized modes on a Drude-like electronic background. Leveraging these effects, we realize all-silicon photoconductive detectors operating at 1.55 μm and room temperature, with a maximum bias-assisted responsivity of 0.58 A/W at 0.5 V. This response arises from plasmon-enhanced sub-bandgap absorption combined with trap-assisted photoconductive gain and therefore does not represent the intrinsic quantum efficiency. These results extend the spectral functionality of silicon photonics beyond its intrinsic absorption limits for integrated sensing, imaging, and optical communication.

articles.title: Geometrically and chemically dual-adaptive COFs for selective recognition of multiple uranium species in complex waters

Multitechnique Characterization
of Dissolved Organic
Matter from Naturally Acidic and Circumneutral Waters Reveals Molecular
Controls on Organic Nitrogen Speciation
articles.abstract: Abstract The molecular characteristics of dissolved organic matter (DOM) vary across seasons, catchments, and land uses, highlighting the need for generalized structure–function relationships that can predict intrinsic DOM bioavailability. This study characterized DOM from naturally acidic (pH 4.3–5.7) and circumneutral (pH 6.8–8.3) freshwaters over two seasons: winter-spring (WS) and summer-autumn (SA) using multiple characterization techniques (optical, fluorescence, targeted LC-MS/MS, 13C NMR, and FTIR). DOM from acidic environments was higher in aromaticity, more humic-like, with a higher C:N ratio but with a greater percentage of nitrogen in the form of amino acids (i.e., DCAA-N%). Seasonality was only observed for neutral samples, with differences between WS and SA dominated by a decrease in nominal molecular weight (MWn) in SA, likely driven by photochemical disaggregation. FTIR analysis indicates that neutral DOM has a higher amide group abundance than acidic DOM despite the lower DCAA-N%, suggesting the dominance of nonproteinaceous amide-N. Very strong dependencies were observed for dissolved organic nitrogen (DON) speciation against aromaticity (SUVA254) and an FTIR-derived ratio of deprotonated carboxylic:aromatic groups, describing the relative hydrophilicity–hydrophobicity of the DOM environment. These parameters largely explain the DCAA distribution and may provide a more generalized way of characterizing DOM that could be applied across different aquatic ecosystems.

articles.title:
Toward
Dynamic Biointerface Toxicology of Micro- and
Nanoplastics Using Organoids and Organ-on-a-Chip Models
articles.abstract: Abstract Micro- and nanoplastic (MNP) toxicity depends on the exposure conditions under which particles encounter biological tissues, yet nominal material descriptors alone do not resolve these conditions. Environmental transformation, biomolecular adsorption, aggregation, and chemical release can alter particle delivery and biological interactions. This Review evaluates these processes alongside evidence from organoids and organ-on-a-chip models, distinguishing direct MNP findings from analogue studies and demonstrations of platform capability. We propose exposure identity as an analytical framework connecting particle history and state with tissue encounter and subsequent processing over time. The synthesis examines what available studies establish about tissue access, barrier responses, distal relay, and susceptibility, and where interpretation remains constrained by exposure characterization or unresolved mechanisms. Human-derived models provide opportunities to investigate tissue-specific responses, but neither biological complexity nor perfusion establishes environmental representativeness or predictive validity. We identify measurement and control requirements for separating particle transfer from chemical release and tissue-derived signaling, interpreting absent effects, and evaluating heterogeneous exposures. Priorities include traceable delivered-dose measurements, synchronized exposure and response sampling, targeted mechanistic tests, and independent validation for a defined use. The proposed framework organizes evidence and testable relationships while retaining uncertainty about generalization to human exposure and health outcomes.

articles.title:
Missed
Opportunities Forgo One-Third of Mass Timber’s
Carbon Storage Potential
articles.abstract: Abstract Building materials are increasingly positioned as a scalable option for carbon dioxide removal (CDR). Carbon-storing engineered wood products, such as structural mass timber, will be instrumental for CDR. However, system-level perspectives can overlook operational choices that forfeit storage potential. Using stage-resolved life-cycle inventories, scenario-aware uncertainty analysis, and dynamic carbon accounting, we trace carbon flows across mass timber supply chains in the United States, from harvest slash and mill residue to wood products through end-of-life. Across modeled deployment scenarios, we show that management decisions, not technical limits, cut 1.4–2.6 gigatons (Gt) of CO2e storage by 2120, corresponding to roughly one-third of mass timber’s storage potential. Globally, storage losses from these choices could reach 3.8–12 Gt CO2e. We outline a storage-first pathway including slash pyrolysis, diversion of mill residue from bioenergy to wood panel markets, and reuse or pyrolysis at end-of-life. Together, these strategies redirect carbon into value-added, long-lived pools rather than short-lived fates, showing that release timing and supply chain routing choices can matter more than production decarbonization in shaping warming outcomes under mass timber deployment. If implemented, these choices recover forgone storage and aid in developing the built environment as a durable carbon reservoir.

articles.title:
Zeolite-Regulated
Electron-Rich Cu–O–Ce
Sites for Efficient Denitrification against Alkali/Heavy Metal Poisoning
articles.abstract: Abstract Enhancing the wide-temperature-window deNOx activity of catalysts under alkali/heavy metal poisoning conditions remains a pivotal challenge in the field of environmental catalysis. To tackle this issue, we designed a novel CuCeOx/ZSM-5 catalyst using an acid-rich zeolite-modulated electron-enriched metal site strategy. This strategy enables the contact between strong acid sites and Cu–O–Ce active sites, simultaneously regulating the efficient NH3–SCR temperature window and enhancing K/Pb poisoning resistance. Compared to CuCeOx, the engineered acid-rich interface significantly facilitates electron transfer from ZSM-5 to CuCeOx, generating electron-rich Cu–O–Ce active sites. These sites not only serve as adjacent adsorption and activation centers for reactants but also inhibit NH3 oxidation, and CuCeOx/ZSM-5 catalyst achieves >90% deNOx efficiency over a wide temperature range of 180–410 °C (T90 = 180–410 °C). K deactivates the catalyst mainly by reducing surface acidity and promoting the accumulation of less-reactive nitrate species, while Pb primarily suppresses Ce4+ → Ce3+ reduction via inducing Cu2+ → Cu+ conversion and occupying CeO2 oxygen vacancies. Notably, the poisoned CuCeOx/ZSM-5 catalyst still retains satisfactory deNOx performance, with the T90 = 230–380 °C. This work not only provides novel mechanistic insights into the deactivation pathways of NH3–SCR catalysts by alkali and heavy metal ions but also offers a viable strategy for the rational design of high-performance, poisoning-tolerant NH3–SCR catalysts tailored for complex flue gas environments.

articles.title:
Solar-Driven Cu(II)–Cu(III)
Redox Cycle on
Decahedral BiVO4 for Scalable Water Purification
articles.abstract: Abstract Conventional Fenton-like reactions rely on external oxidants to generate reactive oxygen species (ROS, e.g., high-valent metal-oxo species (HVMS)), a practice that is inherently unsustainable for water purification. Here, we propose a solar-driven Cu(II)–Cu(III) redox cycle that differs from the traditional view that HVMS generation originates from peroxide-mediated pathways. By tuning the anisotropic built-in field of decahedral BiVO4, photogenerated holes accumulate selectively on its {110} family, enabling hole-driven hydrated Cu(II) oxidation instead of water. This facilitates an oxygen atom transfer (OAT) from adjacent Bi–OH sites to the H-bonded Cu(II) center, stabilizing the Cu(III)-oxo center by forming the Bi–O–Cu(III)–O structure (Cu(III)). Meanwhile, electron-driven dissolved oxygen reduction maintains charge balance. The photosynthetic Cu(III) mediates antibiotic degradation with a rate constant of 0.174 min–1, representing a ∼16-fold enhancement in the degradation rate constant compared to traditional photocatalysis. Crucially, the solar BiVO4 sheet/Cu(II) system sustains consistent up to ∼85% moxifloxacin degradation efficiency in each cycle over 35 days. No total Cu was detected in the effluent of cycling experiments after pH adjustment (∼7.5). These findings provide a new solution to the long-standing challenge of achieving peroxide-free HVMS synthesis and scalable water purification.

articles.title:
Contrasting
Dynamics of Particle-Bound Organophosphate
Esters Reveal Distinct High-Altitude Contaminant Transport Processes
over the Tibetan Plateau
articles.abstract: Abstract Particle-bound semivolatile organic compounds (SVOCs) reaching high-mountain regions are commonly interpreted in terms of temperature-driven gas-particle partitioning and precipitation scavenging. To investigate these competing dynamics, we report year-round, synchronous measurements of particle-bound organophosphate esters (OPEs) in PM2.5 at two contrasting Tibetan Plateau sites: a southern Himalayan receptor (QOMS) and an inland background site (NAMORS). ΣOPEs averaged 111 ± 125 pg m–3 at QOMS and 20 ± 17 pg m–3 at NAMORS, exhibiting a counterintuitive warm-season maximum. This warm-season peak coincided with a 72–91% decline in hygroscopic secondary inorganic aerosols, indicating that trans-Himalayan transport sustains substantial particle-bound OPE inputs during the monsoon despite intense wet deposition. Furthermore, chlorinated congeners with stronger particle association (TCPP, TDCPP) dominated at both sites (TCEP/TCPP = 0.09–0.46). This contrasts with the highly volatile TCEP-dominated profiles reported for Arctic aerosols. Such a difference is consistent with an orographic modulation favoring particulate-phase retention during the shorter trans-Himalayan ascent. However, the lack of simultaneous gas-phase data and potential differences in regional emission histories must also be acknowledged. Back-trajectory clustering and principal component analysis both point to South Asian source regions as the principal control at QOMS. Consequently, correlations of OPEs with temperature and precipitation are better read as proxies for monsoon transport intensity than as evidence of local thermodynamic partitioning. Continued transboundary input suggests that particle-bound OPEs may contribute to deposition and subsequent accumulation in the alpine cryosphere, highlighting the urgent need to incorporate transboundary transport pathways into regional contaminant assessments.

articles.title:
Organophosphate
Flame Retardants Induce Neurodegenerative
Pathologies by Paralyzing HSP90AB1 Chaperone Function: A Multi-Scale
Computational and Biophysical Study
articles.abstract: Abstract This study integrated computational toxicology with biophysical and cellular validation to investigate the neurotoxic potential of 10 flame-retardant-related compounds. ADMETlab 3.0 predicted blood-brain barrier probabilities of 0.989 for bis(1,3-dichloro-2-propyl) phosphate and 0.444 for diphenyl phosphate (DPHP), interpreted as screening predictions. Network topology analysis identified HSP90AB1 as a shared candidate hub target linking organophosphate flame retardants to Alzheimer’s and Parkinson’s diseases. Molecular dynamics simulations indicated a stable HSP90AB1 backbone in the DPHP complex (root-mean-square deviation ∼0.18 nm). Surface plasmon resonance measured an equilibrium dissociation constant of 1.49 μM. DPHP induced dose-dependent cytotoxicity in neuronal cells; the half-maximal inhibitory concentration was not determined within the tested range. HSP90AB1 overexpression mitigated DPHP-induced reactive oxygen species production and transcriptional upregulation of pro-apoptotic and pro-inflammatory genes. Single-cell virtual knockout identified candidate regulatory processes; Parkinson’s disease-related enrichment remained exploratory after multiple-testing correction. Together, the computational, biophysical, and cellular findings support HSP90AB1 as a candidate target of environmental neurotoxicity and motivate further investigation of DPHP.
